sentences.text: Mother of the victim girl lodged a complaint with Women Police Station, Bagalkot stating that her daughter was sitting in the house with a mor os e feeling.
On enquiry, she revealed that she is not interested to pursue the education further and started crying.
4. On further enquiry, she revealed that first accused cajoled her and had a forcible sexual intercour se in the guise of promis e to marry her.
Later on, the said promise turned down to be false.
The matter was taken to th e eld ers of the family and the villag e and panc hayath wa s convened.
Present petitioner is member of the said panchayath.

sentences.text: in the panchayath, he said to have told the main accused that let him not marry come what may.

It is treated as instigation a nd supporting the accused in the incid ent wh ere first a ccused is charged for the offence punishable under Section 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act as admittedly the victim is a minor.
Learned trial Judge after taking cognizance of the matter, h as summoned the present petition as well.
6. Taking cognizance and summoni ng the petitioner is challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

7. Sri K.S.Patil, learned counsel for the petitioner reiterating the grounds urg ed in the petition, at no stretch of imagination, the petitioner can be proceeded for the offence alleged against him inasmuch as he only convened the panchayath a t the request of the complainant and participated in the panchayath and if the main accused failed to marry the victim girl, he cannot be held responsible for the same and alleged allegation that instigated the main accused in directing him not to marry the victim girl
would not amount to any offence whatsoever under the provisions of the POCSO Act and sought for quashing of the pending proceedings.
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader op poses the petition grounds so also Sri Rakesh S.Hattikatagi, learned counsel who appears for the defacto complainant.
9. No doubt, a mere participation in the panchayath at the request of the mother of the victim girl would not ipso facto amou nt to any offence whatsoever especially under the POCSO Act.

10. But in the case on hand, there is specific allegation in the complainant its elf that in the panchayath, present petitioner after hearing both sides, said to have told the main a cc used not to marry the victi m girl come what may.
11. The petitioner is none other tha n th e close relative of the victim family.
So also elder of Lamani community in 'Kupppaldinni Tanda'.

Being the elder of the community, even if he is asked to mediate the differences between the parties, taking note of the fact that the victim girl is a minor, the matter could n ot have been sorted ou t amicably NC: 2023:KHC-D:7524 outside the Court as the offences under the POCSO Act are grievous in nature.
12. Nevertheless, if the petitioner has instigated the main accu sed in not marrying the victim girl or not has to be established during the trial.

Petitioner has to properly explain the incrimina ting materials at the time of recording the accused statement and also by furnishing his explanation if any un der Section 313(5) of Cr.P.C.
13.
It is too premature for this Court to reach such a stage and accept the explanation of the petitioner and quash the pending cri minal proceedings.

sentences.text: Sinc e the petitioner is already on bail, there i s no oth er way for the petitioner excep t to face the trial and put forth his explanation if any before the Trial Court and prove his innocence.

15. Expressing any opinion about the said aspect of the matter at this sta ge by this Court by holding a mini trial would n ot only hamper the NC: 2023:KHC-D:7524 interest of th e prosecution but also it may indirectly affect the rights of the petitioner as well.
16.
Accordingly, desisting from holding mini trial, this Court is of the considered opinion that the grounds urged in the petition are hardly su fficient to admit the matter for further consideration.
17. Hence, the following order is passed:
ORDE R
Admission declined, petition dismissed.
